page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the ecs.g5 family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

In terms of performance, the instance exhibits a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, place the processor in the bottom 25% of performance. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also register weak to poor results. However, when utilizing all 32 physical cores, the multi-core performance rises to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached operations remains consistently in the middle tier.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the ecs.g5.8xlarge is defined by its dedicated resource allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. While single-threaded performance is limited, the 32 dedicated physical cores offer stable, predictable multi-threaded throughput without resource contention. This makes the instance suitable for workloads that can parallelize tasks effectively, such as multi-threaded database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference, rather than single-threaded processing pipelines.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this KVM-based instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, but provides a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks indicate weak single-core and single-threaded execution, but multi-core and multi-threaded operations, such as Passmark CPU tests and Redis SET operations, consistently achieve average tier results. The instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for parallelized workloads where dedicated core allocation prevents resource contention. It is best suited for multi-threaded database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
